metadata.title: Case Studies: Protest and Securitisation in Australia
metadata.description: Legal cases documenting the prosecution, policing, and constitutional adjudication of protest activity in Australia, 2003–2026.
metadata.disclaimer: This dataset is intended as a research and reference tool. It does not constitute legal advice. Users should verify current case law through official sources.

cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales
cases.protest_context: Street protest concerning refugee policy near the Immigration Minister's residence.
cases.main_issue: Whether to prohibit a notified public assembly under Part 4 of the Summary Offences Act 1988 (NSW).
cases.charges: N/A — s 25 application for prohibition order (Summary Offences Act 1988)

cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales
cases.protest_context: Proposed protest near a police officer's home, framed as an anti-police corruption protest.
cases.main_issue: Whether the court should prohibit the assembly where the organiser's purpose was found to be largely vindictive.
cases.charges: N/A — s 25 application for prohibition order (Summary Offences Act 1988)

cases.court: High Court of Australia
cases.protest_context: Street political protest / pamphleteering against police corruption in Townsville.
cases.main_issue: Whether the insulting-words offence could validly burden political communication in the protest context.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed in substance; leading implied-freedom protest / street-speech authority.
cases.charges: Using insulting words (Vagrancy Act s 7(1)(d)); assaulting police; obstructing police

cases.case_name: New South Wales Commissioner of Police v Bainbridge
cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales
cases.protest_context: Proposed protest around the 2007 APEC meeting in Sydney.
cases.main_issue: Whether to prohibit a public assembly in the context of major international security arrangements.
cases.outcome: Police prohibition order granted; the judgment also noted that a prohibition order does not itself criminalise protest.
cases.charges: N/A — s 25 application for prohibition order (Summary Offences Act 1988)

cases.court: Federal Court of Australia
cases.protest_context: Occupy Melbourne encampment in City Square.
cases.main_issue: Urgent challenge to council action affecting the protest occupation.
cases.outcome: Interlocutory relief proceedings concerning removal / enforcement against the occupation.
cases.charges: N/A — constitutional and human rights challenge (Occupy Melbourne)

cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales

cases.court: Supreme Court of Victoria
cases.protest_context: Protest involving painting over a bus-shelter advertisement.
cases.main_issue: Whether Charter free-expression arguments protected protest-related property damage.
cases.outcome: Charter arguments did not protect property damage; the protester was unsuccessful.
cases.charges: Property damage (painting over advertisement with water-soluble paint, cost $47.17)

cases.case_name: Caripis v Victoria Police (Health and Privacy)
cases.court: Victorian Civil and Administrative Tribunal
cases.protest_context: Retention of climate-protest footage by Victoria Police.
cases.main_issue: Whether police retention and use of protest-related footage breached privacy obligations.
cases.outcome: VCAT found against Victoria Police on health/privacy issues related to the protest footage.
cases.charges: N/A — privacy complaint (Health Records Act / Information Privacy Act)

cases.court: High Court of Australia
cases.protest_context: Anti-logging / forestry blockade protest litigation.
cases.main_issue: Whether Tasmania's anti-protest forestry laws impermissibly burdened the implied freedom of political communication.
cases.outcome: Key provisions of the anti-protest law were invalidated.
cases.charges: Failing to comply with police direction to leave forestry area (Workplaces (Protection from Protesters) Act 2014 (Tas))

cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales

cases.court: Court of Appeal of New South Wales

cases.main_issue: Whether procedural / notice issues required reversal of the first-instance outcome.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed on narrow notice/procedural grounds; the Court of Appeal did not re-do the underlying discretionary balancing exercise.
cases.charges: N/A — appeal of prohibition order (Summary Offences Act 1988 s 25)

cases.case_name: EH v Queensland Police Service; GS v Queensland Police Service
cases.court: District Court of Queensland
cases.protest_context: Climate-protest prosecutions involving dangerous attachment / railway obstruction style offences.

cases.charges: Obstructing railway; trespassing on railway; using dangerous attachment device; contravening police direction

cases.outcome: Parts of the anti-protest law were held invalid.
